title: Session with Tiny Parham in Chicago
summary: He played a couple of dates and recorded Um Ta Da Da Da with Tiny Parham, his second recording, without really working with the band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, so you had your own band, at the Dreamland, which you had inherited?
Yes.
Actually.
Yes.
And, what was the next step, then, after that?
Well, --
Was it Tiny Parham --
Well, during the time I was there at the Dreamland I played with Tiny Parham, I think) a couple of dates.
Yes, you did a record called, 'Um Ta Da Da Da.'
That's right.
But was that recorded in St. Paul?
No that was recorded in Chicago.
Was recorded in Chicago?
Oh, yes.
The -(unintelligible) was St. Paul.
No, because I was never definitely in St. Paul with Tiny Parham.
Now was it Bob Butler who was the vocalist there, who was he?
You know I don't know -- I wouldn't even.
Or Homer Hobson?
Homer Hobson was a cornet player with Al Williams at the time. He may have been in there, he may have been with -- I don't know anyone in that band.
No, because it was -- you know, I wasn't too interested.
You didn't really work with a band then?
No I wasn't -- worked with a band. I only did --
Did sessions.
Yes.
Was that your second record session?
That must've been my second recording, yes.
